usage: Parses NTFS metadata files: $MFT, the $J change journal, $Boot, $SDS and $I30. Use it to build file system timelines and to see file creation, deletion and rename activity. It is heavy on disk and memory, so it runs alone.
limitation: The MFT reuses records of deleted files and the $J journal rolls over, so older activity may be gone. Timestamps can be altered (timestomping).

parameters.label: NTFS file
parameters.description: File to process ($MFT | $J | $Boot | $SDS | $I30).

parameters.label: $MFT for $J
parameters.description: $MFT file to use when -f points to a $J file (resolves parent paths in $J CSV output).
Directory to save CSV formatted results to. This or --json is required unless --de or --body is specified.
Directory to save JSON formatted results to. This or --csv is required unless --de or --body is specified.

parameters.label: Bodyfile output folder
parameters.description: Directory to save bodyfile formatted results to. --bdl is also required.

parameters.label: Bodyfile file name
parameters.description: File name to save body formatted results to. When present, overrides default name.

parameters.label: Bodyfile drive letter
parameters.description: Drive letter (C, D, etc.) to use with bodyfile. Only the drive letter itself should be provided.

parameters.label: Bodyfile LF newlines
parameters.description: Use LF vs CRLF for newlines.

parameters.label: Dump FILE record to
parameters.description: Directory to save exported $MFT FILE record. --do is also required.

parameters.label: FILE record offset
parameters.description: Offset of the $MFT FILE record to dump as decimal or hex. Ex: 5120 or 0x1400.

parameters.label: Dump entry details
parameters.description: Dump full details for $MFT entry/sequence #. Format is 'Entry' or 'Entry-Seq' as decimal or hex. Example: 5, 624-5 or 0x270-0x5.

parameters.label: List directory contents
parameters.description: Display contents of the directory specified by --de. Ignored when --de points to a file.

parameters.label: Dump Security Id
parameters.description: Dump full details for Security Id from $SDS as decimal or hex. Example: 624 or 0x270.

parameters.label: Include DOS names
parameters.description: Include DOS file name types in $MFT output.

parameters.label: File listing
parameters.description: Generate condensed file listing of parsed $MFT contents. Requires --csv.

parameters.label: All timestamps
parameters.description: Include all timestamps from 0x30 attribute vs only when they differ from 0x10 in the $MFT.

parameters.label: Recover slack
parameters.description: Recover slack space from FILE records when processing $MFT files.

parameters.label: Dump resident files
parameters.description: Dump $MFT resident files to the --csv or --json directory, in a 'Resident' subdirectory.

parameters.label: Include resident data
parameters.description: Include resident data in JSON/CSV output.

parameters.label: Resident data extensions
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of extensions to include for resident data. If omitted, includes all.

parameters.label: Resident data max size
parameters.description: Maximum size in bytes for resident data to include (max: 1024000).
Process all Volume Shadow Copies that exist on the drive specified by -f (live system, requires Administrator).
Deduplicate -f & VSCs based on SHA-1. First file found wins.
